name: MS-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +14 Republican partisan lean
Incumbent Guest has a large fundraising and cash-on-hand advantage
No polls and no expert ratings; little evidence of Democratic traction
Prediction markets price the race at roughly 98% Republican
model.rationale: The district's +14 Republican lean, Guest's incumbency and roughly five-to-one fundraising edge over Michael Chiaradio, and markets pricing the race near 98% Republican all point the same way. With no polls or ratings showing Democratic strength, the forecast stays firmly in Republican territory.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving Guest would be the main things that could narrow this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Michael Guest, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a Mississippi district that leans about fourteen points Republican. His Democratic challenger, Michael Chiaradio, has raised just over $155,000 and has limited cash on hand, while Guest has raised more than $800,000 and holds a large war chest. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 98 percent.

The fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, Guest's incumbency advantage, and his financial edge all point toward a comfortable Republican margin. The forecast expects a double-digit Republican win, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling in the district.
